title: Coefficient cocycle for the ambient proper-comparison mate
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and unital maps $A\xrightarrow{\varphi}B\xrightarrow{\psi}C$ of finite commutative rings annihilated by powers of $\ell$. Use the ordinary uncompleted constant-ring module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], the geometric derived adjunctions [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], and write $T_T^{A,B}=(-)\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ and $\alpha_{T,E}:T_T^{B,C}T_T^{A,B}E\xrightarrow{\sim}T_T^{A,C}E$ for scalar extension and associativity [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]. Let $q:Z\to Y$ be any scheme morphism. Let $\gamma_{q,E}^{A,B}:T_Y^{A,B}Rq_{*,A}E\to Rq_{*,B}T_Z^{A,B}E$ be precisely the counit mate of [def-sp-reduction-direct-image-comparison]. For every $E\in D(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$,
$$\gamma_{q,E}^{A,C}\circ\alpha_{Y,Rq_{*,A}E}
=Rq_{*,C}(\alpha_{Z,E})\circ\gamma_{q,T_Z^{A,B}E}^{B,C}\circ T_Y^{B,C}(\gamma_{q,E}^{A,B}).$$
This equality is natural in $E$. Neither properness of $q$, boundedness of $E$, nor flatness or finite projective dimension of the coefficient maps is required.

proof.text: Put $\mathscr Y=\operatorname{Sh}(Y_{\mathrm{proet}})$, $\mathscr X=\operatorname{Sh}(Z_{\mathrm{proet}})$ and $u=q_{\mathrm{proet}}$. These are the small-site geometric operations of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. For $R=A,B,C$, [lem-pur-proetale-constant-coefficient-comparison] gives the specified isomorphism $c_R:u^{-1}R_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}R_Z$. Its definition in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] shows that $c_B\circ u^{-1}(\varphi_Y)=\varphi_Z\circ c_A$, and likewise for $\psi$: the adjoints send each constant section $a$ to the same constant section $\varphi(a)$ on the base change. The maps on locally constant sections follow by restriction and gluing, and then by sheafification. Thus the coefficient sheaves and both coefficient maps on $Z$ are precisely the inverse images of those on $Y$, identified through the specified $c_R$. Transporting module actions through these ring isomorphisms is the identified-coefficient convention already built into the prescribed operations; it introduces no new choice of adjunction.

proof.text:
Identify the scalar associators before using the general cocycle. On either site choose a flat-term K-flat representative $P\to N$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The comparison $\tau_T$ of [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization] is represented by
$$(P\otimes_{A_T}B_T)\otimes_{B_T}C_T\longrightarrow P\otimes_{A_T}C_T,\qquad (x\otimes b)\otimes c\longmapsto x\otimes\psi(b)c.$$
Its inverse inserts $1_B$. This is exactly the canonical tensor associativity used for $\alpha_{T,N}$ in [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor], whose scalar extension is computed by the same K-flat model, including the action through the right factor. Hence $\tau_T=\alpha_T$, with the direction from iterated extension to direct extension. This verification applies to every $N$ by the representative isomorphism and naturality. The normalization theorem already supplies the validity of the iterated K-flat computation for arbitrary ring maps; no flatness of $B$ over $A$ or $C$ over $B$ is inferred.

Write $P_R=q_R^*$, $G_R=Rq_{*,R}$ and $\lambda^{R,S}:P_ST_Y^{R,S}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_Z^{R,S}P_R$. In [def-sp-reduction-direct-image-comparison], $\lambda$ is the balanced K-flat tensor/pullback map, so under the coefficient identifications of step 1 it is the canonical inverse-image/tensor comparison in [lem-pur-ringed-coefficient-projection-cocycle]. Both send the inverse image of $x\otimes s$ to the inverse image of $x$ tensor $s$, and use the same normalized geometric adjunction [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. For $R\to S$ equal to any of $A\to B$, $B\to C$ or $A\to C$, the specified mate is consequently characterized by
$$\varepsilon^S_{T_Z^{R,S}E}\circ P_S(\gamma^{R,S}_{q,E})=T_Z^{R,S}(\varepsilon^R_E)\circ\lambda^{R,S}_{G_RE}.$$
The adjunct-counit equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity] makes this characterization unique. It is exactly the defining transpose of $\chi$ in the cited general cocycle, so $\chi_\varphi=\gamma^{A,B}_q$, $\chi_\psi=\gamma^{B,C}_q$ and $\chi_{\psi\varphi}=\gamma^{A,C}_q$. This checks equality of the specified maps, not only existence of some comparison.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-pur-ringed-coefficient-projection-cocycle] to $u$ and the three ring sheaves $A_Y\to B_Y\to C_Y$. Step 1 checks its inverse-image coefficient hypothesis; the derived categories are ordinary unbounded module categories as required. Its identity is
$$\chi_{\psi\varphi,E}\circ\tau_{Y,G_AE}=G_C(\tau_{Z,E})\circ\chi_{\psi,T_Z^{A,B}E}\circ T_Y^{B,C}(\chi_{\varphi,E}).$$
Substitute $\tau=\alpha$ from step 2 and $\chi=\gamma$ from step 3. With $G_R=Rq_{*,R}$ this is exactly the required displayed equality, as an equality in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},C)$. Its common source is $T_Y^{B,C}T_Y^{A,B}G_AE$, and its common target is $G_CT_Z^{A,C}E$.

proof.text: The equation supplied by [lem-pur-ringed-coefficient-projection-cocycle] is an identity of natural transformations, so evaluating it gives the asserted equality for every $E$ and its naturality in every morphism $E\to E'$. That node works with arbitrary unbounded objects and arbitrary sheaf ring maps, and explicitly assumes neither flatness nor invertibility of the comparison. Its geometric morphism is arbitrary. Thus the specialization uses no properness of $q$, boundedness of $E$, or flatness or finite projective dimension of either coefficient map. The finite $\ell$-power coefficient hypotheses in the item merely restrict the allowed rings.

lean.statement: theorem proEtaleDirectImageScalarCocycle (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] {A B C : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C] [Finite A] [Finite B] [Finite C] (_hA : ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ a : A, (ℓ ^ n) • a = 0) (_hB : ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ b : B, (ℓ ^ n) • b = 0) (_hC : ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ c : C, (ℓ ^ n) • c = 0) (φ : A →+* B) (ψ : B →+* C) {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (q : Z ⟶ Y) (E : Scheme.proEtaleDerivedCategory Z A) : (scalarExtensionFunctor_composition φ ψ Y).hom.app ((directImageConstantPush A q).obj E) ≫ (directImageScalarComparison (ψ.comp φ) q).app E = (scalarExtensionFunctor ψ Y).map ((directImageScalarComparison φ q).app E) ≫ (directImageScalarComparison ψ q).app ((scalarExtensionFunctor φ Z).obj E) ≫ (directImageConstantPush C q).map ((scalarExtensionFunctor_composition φ ψ Z).hom.app E)
